overview: This pairs a slotted disc (mounted on a motor shaft or wheel axle) with a small IR emitter/receiver module that straddles it — as the disc spins, its slots alternately let light through and block it, producing a pulse train the microcontroller can count. Counting pulses over time gives speed; counting total pulses gives distance traveled, closing the loop that an open-loop DC motor alone can't provide (a DC motor has no idea how far it's actually turned — it just knows the voltage applied to it). Two-channel ('quadrature') versions add a second sensor offset from the first, letting software also determine rotation direction, not just speed.
simpleSummary: A sensor that counts wheel or shaft rotations by watching light pass through a slotted disc.

specifications.outputType: Digital pulse train (single-channel) or quadrature pulses (dual-channel, adds direction sensing)
specifications.resolution: Depends on slot count on the disc (common range: 20-100 slots per revolution)
specifications.sensingPrinciple: IR emitter/receiver pair interrupted by a slotted disc

pinMap.name: VCC
pinMap.function: Power input for the IR emitter/receiver pair.

pinMap.name: OUT A
pinMap.function: Primary pulse output — one pulse per slot passing through the sensor.
pinMap.gotcha: At high wheel speeds, pulses arrive fast enough that polling in the main loop misses some — use a hardware interrupt pin to count reliably.

pinMap.name: OUT B
pinMap.function: Second pulse output, phase-offset from OUT A on quadrature (2-channel) encoders — comparing the two determines rotation direction.
pinMap.gotcha: Only present on 2-channel/quadrature versions — single-channel encoders can measure speed but not direction.

useCases.title: Closed-loop wheeled robot odometry
useCases.scenario: Track exact distance traveled and correct for wheel slip/motor variance between left and right wheels.

useCases.title: Precise motor speed control (PID)
useCases.scenario: Feed real-time speed feedback into a PID control loop for accurate speed regulation.

oftenConfusedWith: Rotary encoder (a manual control knob, not a motor-feedback sensor)
Hall effect sensor (can serve a similar speed-sensing role using a magnet instead of a slotted disc)
oftenUpgradedTo: Magnetic absolute encoders for higher precision and no optical-alignment sensitivity
